Anthropic released the Claude 4 family, consisting of two models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The release was structured to serve distinct market segments with specific pricing tiers: Opus 4 served as the flagship model priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens, while Sonnet 4 acted as a fast workhorse priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1]. This dual-model strategy positioned Sonnet 4 specifically as the developer-default coding model [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled that agentic coding had become the defining product focus of 2025, driven by the rise of Claude Code [Source: ev-1]. By introducing "computer use 2.0," which was roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation's capabilities, Anthropic emphasized reliability and safety in its positioning against competitors like the OpenAI o-series during an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush [Source: ev-1]. The market response to this signal was significant; driven by Claude Code adoption, Anthropic reported record API usage and subsequently raised a large funding round at a valuation of approximately $183 billion, cementing its position as the coding-agent leader [Source: ev-1].
